answer: Give every identity a maturing kernel of trust: a new agent earns nothing until it survives weeks of liveness check-ins, each demanding a signed response within a short window, like crossing a canyon on a bridge that cannot be rushed. Rewards are back-loaded, so weight grows only after presence, and a missed check-in resets the clock. A Sybil farmer in the tundra of cheap accounts must keep thousands of identities awake for months, paying compute and attention, while one operator cannot answer simultaneous challenges across them all. Time, not just money, becomes the cost of cloning.
